international.title: Burnham should ‘move on’ from Brexit, says Theresa May, as critics hit out over closer EU ties – UK politics live
international.summary: Issue dominates Sunday broadcast round following Friday’s deals on trade and youth mobility Theresa May ‘aghast’ at Andy Burnham’s talk about rejoining EU Foreign secretary Ed Miliband on the BBC was also pressed on the business argument that cutting EU red tape on food and agricultural trade will make a grocery shop cheaper. Kuennsberg raises the statement from the British Retail Consortium which says that the deals to cut red tape on food and agricultural products will “reduce pressure on trading costs” but are “unlikely to have any impact on prices in the near future” as “most of our food already comes from the United Kingdom.” And this deal will make a positive impact on both exports and imports, and crucially- this is the point that I noticed the retailers were making - it will reduce the costs that the retailers face, all of that Brexit red tape, millions of forms that they were having to fill in, frankly, pointlessly, as a result of the bad deals that we had. If people think the status quo is really good on Brexit and that that’s been great for Britain, well, they won’t like this deal. I think most people think the status quo has been actually pretty rubbish. And we need to make it better and that is what this deal does.” Continue reading...
